title: About
text:
The idea for DIV was born from the recognition that Chicagoland is home to a wealth of researchers in human–data interaction and data visualization and that we all benefit from more regular connection across institutions.
In 2025 a small gathering of visualization faculty and PhD students from Northwestern, U Chicago, and DePaul held a one-day retreat hosted by Northwestern’s MU Collective. We had so much fun connecting that we did it again in 2026, adding in folks from UIC and Argonne, hosted at U Chicago’s Data Science Institute.
At the 2026 retreat we recognized the need for more opportunities like this: venues where students, faculty, and researchers can talk about ongoing work and get honest feedback. Venues where we can discuss hard topics, like where the field is, where it’s going, and where it should be going. But also, importantly, venues where we can connect socially to local folks and build longer-lasting collaborations and friendships.
For 2027, we’re expanding the topic from visualization to human–data interaction. We hope folks will join us and have fun making new connections and building new collaborations!

title: Data Interaction and Visualization 2027
text:
DIV 2027 is a symposium for academic and industry researchers in the greater Chicago area working in fields related to human-data interaction. Our focus is the use of data representations such as visualization, language, and statistics to aid processing, understanding, and communicating data. The goal of the workshop is to promote connection and collaboration amongst the local and regional community, and especially to give early researchers (including graduate students) a venue to build academic networks and get feedback on their work.

title: Data Interaction and Visualization 2027
text:
Posters
All attendees – including faculty, researchers, postdocs, and students – are invited to submit a poster for presentation at the workshop.
Students are especially encouraged to submit. We aim to provide a space for well-considered, thoughtful feedback on work of all stages, but especially unfinished or in-progress work that can most benefit from feedback and discussion.

Submission
Submit a poster abstract using this Google Form by November 30, 2026.
Poster information:

Abstract length: ≤ 250 words.
Suggested poster size: 24 in × 36 in.
Lightning talk: Poster presenters will give a 1 minute lightning talk before the poster session to advertise their poster.
Work stage: Posters may cover already-published work or work in progress.
Archivalness: Posters and abstracts are non-archival.
